title: Page the SDDC Manager credentials collection into a stable, completely retrieved list
prompt:
Implement `SddcCredentialsClient.java` as a single-file, JDK-only client for one VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager workflow: sign in, then read the whole paginated credentials collection and hand it back in one stable order.

Start by reading the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json`. That focused contract was projected straight out of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0` (commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`, blob `ff648cdf010715649b607f0edfa480b2c515e2a9`). The JSON specification at that tag is authoritative here - not a rendered documentation portal, and not the different revision of the same file that ships at the 9.1.0.0 tag. Use only the operationIds `createToken` and `getCredentials`.

Keep the public surface in `SddcCredentialsClient.java` exactly as declared - `TestMain` compiles against it. The constructor already stores the base URL and the `HttpClient` and does no I/O.

`authenticateWithPassword(username, password)` and `authenticateWithApiKey(apiKey)` both drive `createToken`:

- POST to `{baseUrl}/v1/tokens` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: application/json`, and without an Authorization header - this call is what establishes the session.
- Every property of `TokenCreationSpec` is optional. Send only the properties the caller actually supplied: the password grant puts `username` and `password` on the wire and nothing else, the api key grant puts `apiKey` on the wire and nothing else. An unset property must be absent from the JSON object, not present as `""` or `null`.
- A 201 carries a `TokenPair`; keep its `accessToken` for subsequent calls.

`listCredentials(resourceType, pageSize)` reads the collection:

- Without a prior successful `createToken` it throws `IllegalStateException`, and a `pageSize` below 1 throws `IllegalArgumentException`. Both must happen before anything is put on the wire - a `pageSize` of 0 would ask the server for one unpaginated page, which defeats the point of this client.
- Each page is a GET to `{baseUrl}/v1/credentials` with `Accept: application/json`, `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`, no request body and no Content-Type. Send `pageNumber` and `pageSize` on every request; send `resourceType` only when the caller passed one - a `null` filter means the parameter is not on the wire at all, not an empty value. Percent-encode values, never repeat a parameter, and never send a parameter with an empty value. Parameter order is not checked.
- Start at `pageNumber=0` and keep going until `pageMetadata.totalPages` pages have been read. Fetch every page exactly once: no re-reads, and no extra probing request past the last page.
- Collect the `elements` of every page, project each into the declared `Credential` record (`resourceId`, `resourceName`, `resourceType` and `domainNames` come from the credential's `resource`; a missing `domainNames` becomes an empty list), then return an unmodifiable list sorted ascending by `resourceName`, then `username`, then `id`, each compared with `String.compareTo`. The server hands pages back in its own order, so the ordering has to be yours.
- Any non-2xx response ends the walk immediately and surfaces as the declared `ApiException`, carrying the HTTP status plus `errorCode` and `message` from the `Error` body.

JDK class library only - no third-party dependencies, no build tool. `Json` is already in the repo for parsing and writing; note that its writer emits a `null` value as JSON `null` rather than dropping the key, so omission is your job.

`TestMain.java` is the acceptance contract. It starts `MockSddcManager`, a loopback stand-in that routes only the operations named in `docs/contract.json`, and then verifies the exact wire shape from that mock's request log. Run `java TestMain.java` from the repository root until it prints `all checks passed`. Only `SddcCredentialsClient.java` may be edited; `TestMain.java`, `MockSddcManager.java`, `Json.java` and everything under `docs/` are protected. Nothing in this task talks to a live VMware endpoint.

prerequisites.java: 22 or later (TestMain is launched in multi-file source mode)

scenario: getCredentials is paged and the server returns pages in inventory order; the client must read every page exactly once and emit the union in one deterministic order (resourceName, username, id) that no single page exhibits.
environment_note: MockSddcManager binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, builds its routing table and its allowed query parameter names from the protected docs/contract.json, and appends every exchange to a JSON Lines request log in a temporary directory that TestMain reads back. No route in the seed reaches a live VMware endpoint.
constraint: The mock serves only createToken and getCredentials and rejects a repeated, unknown or empty-valued query parameter and an empty TokenCreationSpec property, while the harness asserts the request log independently: operation order, paths, exact query parameter name sets, header values, request bodies, and that unset optional fields are omitted from the wire rather than sent empty.
